status: PROPOSED REPORT STRUCTURE / NOT A UNIVERSITY FINDING
description: Machine-readable map of RFQ report element -> report section -> required inputs. The coverage checker in report_structure.py fails closed on an unmapped element, a section with no source, an unknown dataset, or a field absent from the real register schema.

excluded_deliverables.name: Formal audit or compliance opinion
excluded_deliverables.why: This engagement produces an assessment of current practice against reference frameworks used as prompts. It does not issue an audit opinion, a compliance determination, a certification, or an attestation.

excluded_deliverables.name: Employee or individual performance evaluation
excluded_deliverables.why: Findings describe organizational practice, systems and process. No statement rates, ranks or evaluates a named person or role holder.

excluded_deliverables.name: Vendor or product procurement recommendation
excluded_deliverables.why: Recommendations describe capabilities and decisions the University would need to make. Selecting, endorsing or pricing a specific product or vendor is outside this engagement.

rfq_elements.name: Executive summary
rfq_elements.rfq_basis: Leadership-readable summary of what was assessed, what was found, and what is proposed.
rfq_elements.must_not: Must not introduce a statement that no finding supports.

rfq_elements.name: Engagement scope and assessment areas
rfq_elements.rfq_basis: What was in scope: ESS, RIS, IAM across software development, security, deployment/operations, AI readiness.
rfq_elements.must_not: Must not imply coverage of services or areas that were not assessed.

rfq_elements.name: Methodology
rfq_elements.rfq_basis: How evidence was collected, how interviews and artifacts were used, how findings were formed.
rfq_elements.must_not: Must not present the method as an audit procedure or a certification process.

rfq_elements.name: Evidence standard, confidence and limitations
rfq_elements.rfq_basis: The confidence vocabulary, what each class means, and the declared limits of the engagement.
rfq_elements.must_not: Must not average confidence dimensions into a maturity score.

rfq_elements.name: Peer and published-practice context
rfq_elements.rfq_basis: External reference points that help interpret current practice.
rfq_elements.must_not: Must not rank the University against peers or state a percentile.

rfq_elements.name: Current-state findings by group and area
rfq_elements.rfq_basis: The 12-cell ESS|RIS|IAM x SD|SEC|DEP|AI view plus the per-group narrative.
rfq_elements.must_not: Must not convert an unassessed cell into a low rating.

rfq_elements.name: Cross-cutting themes
rfq_elements.rfq_basis: Patterns that span groups or areas, each still traceable to the individual findings it spans.
rfq_elements.must_not: Must not dissolve individual findings into a generic summary.

rfq_elements.name: Group and department recommendations
rfq_elements.rfq_basis: Proposed actions addressed to a named group, each linked to the findings that motivate it.
rfq_elements.must_not: Must not recommend a specific product, vendor, or purchase.

rfq_elements.name: Prioritization and phasing
rfq_elements.rfq_basis: Sequencing of recommendations across 0-90 / 90-180 / 180+ day horizons with visible assumptions.
rfq_elements.must_not: Must not present an estimate that was never supplied as a computed number.

rfq_elements.name: Supporting evidence
rfq_elements.rfq_basis: The evidence items behind every finding, with source locators and scope limits.
rfq_elements.must_not: Must not expose sensitive locators that the engagement agreed to keep controlled.

rfq_elements.name: Source and version register
rfq_elements.rfq_basis: Every external framework and source, pinned to the version actually used.
rfq_elements.must_not: Must not cite a draft framework revision as final practice.

rfq_elements.name: Open questions and unresolved inputs
rfq_elements.rfq_basis: What stayed UNKNOWN, why, and what would resolve it.
rfq_elements.must_not: Must not silently drop an unresolved input to make the report look complete.

sections.title: Executive Summary
sections.purpose: Answer, in one page, what was assessed, what holds up, what does not, and what is proposed next.

required_inputs.why: Every summary statement names the finding_id it rests on.
Proposed next steps, each already linked to findings.
The small number of patterns leadership needs before the detail.

sections.traceability_rule: Every sentence that asserts a condition carries at least one finding_id or theme_id.
sections.unknown_rule: Areas with status UNKNOWN are named here as unassessed, never omitted to make coverage look complete.
prompts: What did we actually look at, and over what window?
Which two or three conditions most affect delivery and risk?
What is proposed in the first 90 days, and what does it depend on?
What could we not determine, and what would settle it?

sections.title: Engagement Scope and Assessment Areas
sections.purpose: State exactly which groups, services and assessment areas were in scope, and which were not.

required_inputs.why: Scope statements grounded in the documented responsibilities of each group.
The assessed cell set; anything outside it is declared out of scope.

sections.traceability_rule: Each in-scope service traces to a source_ids entry confirming the responsibility boundary.
sections.unknown_rule: A service in scope but not reached is listed as in-scope/not-assessed, not quietly dropped.
prompts: Which applications and shared platforms are in scope for each group?
Which assessment areas were covered for each group?
What was explicitly excluded, and why?

sections.title: Methodology
sections.purpose: Describe how evidence was gathered and how findings were formed, so a reader can judge the work.

required_inputs.why: Frameworks used as interview and artifact prompts, with each one's stated adaptation limit.
The actual source mix and collection window, reported rather than asserted.

sections.traceability_rule: Every framework reference cites framework + version + locator.
sections.unknown_rule: Where a planned collection step did not happen, the method section says so.
prompts: What was collected, from whom, over what period?
How were interview statements separated from artifact evidence?
How were framework references used as prompts rather than as criteria?
What is the declared freshness window for volatile evidence?

sections.title: Evidence Standard, Confidence and Limitations
sections.purpose: Define the confidence vocabulary and the limits of what this engagement can support.

required_inputs.why: The five confidence dimensions, reported separately and never averaged.

sections.traceability_rule: Each confidence class shown here matches the definition in the evidence method the register was built against.
sections.unknown_rule: NOT_EVIDENCED and UNRESOLVED are defined as distinct from a negative finding.
prompts: What does each confidence class mean in this report?
Which limits apply to the whole engagement rather than a single finding?
Where did contradictory evidence remain unresolved?

sections.title: Peer and Published-Practice Context
sections.purpose: Offer external reference points that help interpret current practice, with comparability stated.

required_inputs.why: Each peer reference carries its own comparability status and the denominator it was measured against.

sections.traceability_rule: Every peer row displays comparison_status and comparability_notes next to the value.
sections.unknown_rule: A published process target is labeled as intent, not as attained performance.
prompts: What do comparable institutions publish about this practice?
What would have to be normalized before these numbers could be compared?
Which references are context only and cannot support a comparison?

sections.title: Current-State Matrix
sections.purpose: Show all twelve group-by-area cells at once, including the ones that were not assessed.

required_inputs.why: The matrix itself; one row per assessed cell.

sections.traceability_rule: Each populated cell shows its finding_id.
sections.unknown_rule: A cell with status UNKNOWN renders as UNKNOWN - not assessed, is visually distinct from a weak result, and is excluded from every count of assessed cells.
prompts: Which cells are supported, partial, in conflict, or unassessed?
Where does the evidence disagree with itself?

sections.title: Group Findings - Enterprise Systems and Services (ESS)
sections.purpose: Narrative findings for ESS across the four assessment areas.

required_inputs.why: The ESS rows of the matrix.
The observations behind each ESS finding.

sections.traceability_rule: Every narrative claim names its finding_id; every finding names its supporting evidence_ids.
sections.unknown_rule: Where ESS evidence covers one service only, the narrative says so instead of generalizing to the group.
prompts: What holds up across ESS, and on what evidence?
Where is the evidence single-service rather than group-wide?
What follow-up would resolve each partial or conflicting cell?

sections.title: Group Findings - Research Information Systems (RIS)
sections.purpose: Narrative findings for RIS across the four assessment areas.

required_inputs.why: The RIS rows of the matrix.
The observations behind each RIS finding.

sections.traceability_rule: Every narrative claim names its finding_id; every finding names its supporting evidence_ids.
sections.unknown_rule: A policy that documents intent is not reported as demonstrated implementation.
prompts: What holds up across RIS, and on what evidence?
Which RIS claims rest on policy intent rather than observed practice?

sections.title: Group Findings - Identity and Access Management (IAM)
sections.purpose: Narrative findings for IAM across the four assessment areas.

required_inputs.why: The IAM rows of the matrix.
The observations behind each IAM finding.

sections.traceability_rule: Every narrative claim names its finding_id; every finding names its supporting evidence_ids.
sections.unknown_rule: An absent access-review record is reported as no evidence observed, not as a failed control.
prompts: What holds up across IAM, and on what evidence?
Where is an absence of records being read as an absence of practice?

sections.title: Cross-Cutting Themes
sections.purpose: Name the patterns that span groups or areas without erasing the findings underneath them.

required_inputs.why: Each theme cites the exact findings it spans and any evidence that cuts against it.
Used to confirm every cited finding exists and that the span claim matches the matrix.

sections.traceability_rule: A theme cites at least two finding_ids from at least two distinct groups or areas.
sections.unknown_rule: A theme that would require an unassessed cell to hold is stated with that gap named.
prompts: Which conditions recur across groups rather than being local?
What evidence cuts against each theme?
Which findings does this theme deliberately not cover?

sections.title: Recommendations by Group and Department
sections.purpose: Proposed actions addressed to a named owner group, each tied to the findings that motivate it.

required_inputs.why: The recommendation records, each carrying its own finding links and resource note.
Used to show the strength of the evidence a recommendation rests on.

sections.traceability_rule: Every recommendation cites at least one finding_id and does not inherit that finding's confidence automatically.
sections.unknown_rule: A recommendation motivated by an unresolved question is labeled as investigate-first rather than implement.
prompts: What should this group do, and which finding motivates it?
What capability is needed - stated as a capability, not a product?
What does this action depend on before it can start?

sections.title: Prioritization and Phasing
sections.purpose: Sequence the recommendations across the 0-90 / 90-180 / 180+ horizons with the assumptions visible.

required_inputs.why: Horizon and dependency per recommendation, with the resource assumption shown rather than computed away.

sections.traceability_rule: Every phased item links back to a recommendation_id, and no item appears in a phase earlier than its dependency.
sections.unknown_rule: A recommendation with horizon UNKNOWN is listed in an unsequenced bucket with the missing input named, never defaulted into 180+.
prompts: What must happen first because something else depends on it?
Which items are sequenced by evidence rather than by preference?
Which estimates are missing, and what would supply them?

sections.title: Appendix A - Supporting Evidence
sections.purpose: The evidence items behind every finding, so a reviewer can re-open any source.

required_inputs.why: The full register, unabridged, so nothing in the body rests on an item that is not listed here.
Per-change delivery traces where a finding rests on observed change activity.

sections.traceability_rule: Every finding_id cited anywhere in the body appears in this appendix with at least one evidence item.
sections.unknown_rule: An evidence item whose represented_period could not be established keeps recency UNKNOWN rather than being assumed current.
prompts: What exactly did we see, and what does it establish?
What is the scope limit of each source?

sections.title: Appendix B - Source and Version Register
sections.purpose: Pin every external framework and published source to the version actually used.

required_inputs.why: The frozen framework versions and how each was treated.
Policy sources with their applicability caveats intact.

sections.traceability_rule: Every external citation in the body resolves to a row here with a version or review date.
sections.unknown_rule: A draft revision is recorded as a horizon-scan item and is never cited as current practice.
prompts: Which version of each framework was used?
Which sources were accessed on which date?

sections.title: Appendix C - Open Questions and Unresolved Inputs
sections.purpose: Carry forward everything that stayed UNKNOWN, and say what would resolve it.

required_inputs.why: Every cell that is UNKNOWN, PARTIAL or CONFLICT, with the question that would resolve it.
Evidence items left UNRESOLVED or NOT_EVIDENCED, with their follow-up.

sections.traceability_rule: Every UNKNOWN, PARTIAL or CONFLICT cell in the matrix appears here exactly once.
sections.unknown_rule: This section is the reason an absent input never has to become a zero anywhere else in the report.
prompts: What could we not determine?
What specific artifact or access would resolve it?
Who owns supplying it?
